look_here_first: 1) Older trunks have unusually smooth pale gray peeling/mottled bark; 2) leaves are SMALL (often 1.5–3.5 cm), simple, alternate, usually obovate with rolled-under margins and short hairs beneath; 3) immature berries green, RIPE fruits dark purple-black with persistent calyx. Never identify from black fruit alone.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Shrub to small tree, often multistemmed; foliage may be deciduous or persistent depending on site.

key_traits.label: Bark
key_traits.text: Smooth pale gray to reddish-gray bark that exfoliates and creates a mottled trunk.

key_traits.label: Leaves
key_traits.text: Alternate simple leaves, usually small and obovate, glossy/dark above and densely tomentose beneath.

key_traits.label: Reproductive
key_traits.text: White urn-shaped flowers; flowers arise on previous-season twigs and ovaries are pubescent.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Berrylike fruit roughly 1.5–2.5 cm, maturing dark/black and remaining pubescent, with persistent calyx and several seeds.

key_traits.label: Joey field note
key_traits.text: Joey's desert-field frame gives an immediate woody-ID view of Texas persimmon's smooth pale bark and small-tree habit. Use the bark as an early cue, then confirm the small obovate leaves and, when present, the pubescent black fruit.

key_traits.label: Leaf field details
key_traits.text: UT Austin Williamson flora: simple alternate blades approximately 15–35 × 7–16 mm (local specimens), obovate/elliptic, rounded or notched apex, frequently rolled-under (revolute) margin, short-tomentose underside.

key_traits.label: Flower field details
key_traits.text: Small white to cream 5-lobed urn flowers; pollen-producing flowers typically in 1–3-flower clusters, ovary-bearing flowers often solitary. A source conflict exists over dioecious vs monoecious organization; identify flower sex from visible organs rather than assume tree sex.

key_traits.label: Berry field details
key_traits.text: Young fruit green; mature 17–22 mm berry black/dark purple, often hairy, with persistent conspicuous 4–5-lobed calyx and typically several hard brown seeds.
